title: api: schema versioning, beta headers, and backward-compat shims for streaming/tool-calls/structured-output
author: Sofia Chen
description:
Background: As we expand structured output, streaming semantics, and tool/function-calling features, we need a stable way to evolve request/response schemas without breaking existing customers (including users of our OpenAI-compat layer). This PR introduces API schema versioning with an explicit beta header, a server-side handler for v2 semantics, and backward-compatibility shims that translate legacy OpenAI-compatible payloads into the new canonical shapes.

What this changes (summary):
- Adds an explicit API version header for beta testing (X-Redwood-API-Version: v2-beta) and advertises an Accept/Content-Type media-type parameter for clients that prefer content negotiation.
- Introduces v2 canonical schema changes: namespaced tool_call object replacing the legacy function_call enum, a formal structured_output envelope for stream/chunk boundaries, and clearer typing for streaming control frames.
- Implements runtime backward-compatibility shims: the OpenAI-compat adapter now accepts old function_call enum payloads and maps them to the v2 tool_call shape; streaming chunk shapes from older clients are mapped to the new structured_output chunks; unknown extra fields are logged (with rate limits) and preserved in an extensions map.
- Adds feature flag / rollout guard that defaults to off; rollout is controlled by account-level flags (see rollout plan below).
- Documentation updates and migration guide included.

Motivation: We observed several customers relying on ad-hoc OpenAI-compatible payloads; incremental changes to streaming and tool-calling semantics risk silent regressions. Schema versioning allows controlled beta testing and clearer deprecation messaging while shims reduce the blast radius for fast-moving clients.

Design notes:
- Version selection priority: explicit X-Redwood-API-Version header -> Accept media-type parameter -> account-level default -> server default (v1).
- Beta header value is "v2-beta" while GA will be "v2". Clients using v1 will continue to be served by the v1 handler unless explicitly opted-in.
- The new tool_call is an object: {"name": string, "args": object, "metadata": {}}. The adapter will translate legacy function_call: {"name": "foo", "arguments": "{...}"} into the new object, including JSON parsing of string-encoded arguments.
- Streaming: earlier ad-hoc 'chunk_type' strings have been formalized into 'structured_output' control frames with explicit 'boundary' semantics. The runtime now emits canonical chunk metadata for downstream SDKs.
- OpenAI-compat: the compatibility layer is extended with translation tables and tests to ensure round-trip parity for common legacy clients.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for translation logic and schema validation added (see tests/).
- Integration tests covering streaming handshakes and legacy client behavior added.
- Perf runs profiled to ensure shims have negligible overhead (baseline + ~2-4% CPU in worst-case pathological routes).
- Rollout via account opt-in and feature flag; monitoring dashboards added to Console for error rates and translation misses.

Migration path for customers:
- Short term (now): opt-in to v2-beta via the X-Redwood-API-Version header or account flag. SDKs will add helpers to set header automatically.
- Medium term (60 days): customers should migrate to the v2 canonical tool_call and structured_output formats. Deprecation warnings are surfaced in response headers when legacy formats are used.
- Long term (180 days+): v1 will be deprecated; server will stop accepting legacy-only payloads after a deprecation window (final schedule will be announced publicly).

Notes on backward compatibility: Shims are intentionally conservative — we perform tolerant parsing and attach unmapped fields to the extensions map rather than dropping them. This keeps outputs recoverable for downstream tooling while enabling cleaner v2 semantics going forward.

review_comments: Miguel Alvarez: Overall LGTM. Please add a migration note in the SDK changelogs and confirm perf impact for high-throughput routes.
Sofia Chen (author): Added SDK changelog entries and included perf microbenchmarks in the PR description. Perf impact is 2-4% CPU on worst-case paths; typical routes are within noise.
Priya Patel: Can we ensure we don't convert string-encoded json args incorrectly if a user intentionally passes a string? Add a safe parsing option.
Sofia Chen (author): Updated adapter to attempt JSON.parse only when the string looks like an object/array (leading '{' or '[') and otherwise pass as raw string. Added tests.
Kenji Sato: Please add an integration test that simulates a partially-formed legacy stream (missing chunk_type) and ensure the shim doesn't crash the runtime.
Sofia Chen (author): Added the requested integration test and a defensive guard in the streaming parser.
release_notes: Adds API schema versioning with a v2 beta header, introduces canonical v2 tool_call and structured_output shapes, and provides backward-compatibility shims for OpenAI-compatible payloads. Customers can opt into v2-beta via header or account flag; migration guide and SDK updates included. Deprecation window announced in docs.
notes_for_support: Support teams: watch for translation-miss metrics in Console (category: schema_translation_miss). If customers report malformed tool_call payloads, verify whether they are sending historically string-encoded arguments and advise using the SDK helpers or the X-Redwood-API-Version header to opt-in during migration.
